scenarios.title_en: Ordering food: ingredients, allergies and diets
scenarios.title_he: הזמנת אוכל: רכיבים, אלרגיות ותזונה מיוחדת

situation.en: You're having dinner at a busy restaurant in London with a friend who is vegetarian. You're allergic to nuts. The server comes over to take your order.
situation.he: ארוחת ערב במסעדה עמוסה בלונדון, יחד עם חברה צמחונית. יש לך אלרגיה לאגוזים, והמלצרית ניגשת לשולחן כדי לקחת את ההזמנה.

goal.en: Ask what's in a dish, explain your allergy clearly, find a vegetarian option for your friend and order.
goal.he: לשאול ממה מורכבת מנה, להסביר בבירור את האלרגיה, למצוא אפשרות צמחונית לחברה ולהזמין.

phrases.en: What's in the chicken salad?
I'm allergic to nuts. Does this dish have any nuts in it?
phrases.he: יש לי אלרגיה לאגוזים. יש במנה הזאת אגוזים?
phrases.note: Say 'allergic to', not 'allergic for' or 'allergic from'.

phrases.en: It's quite a serious allergy, so could you check with the kitchen?
phrases.he: זו אלרגיה די חמורה, אז אפשר לבדוק עם המטבח?

phrases.en: Do you have any vegetarian options?
Is this suitable for vegetarians?
phrases.note: A phrase you'll often see on British menus and labels.

phrases.en: Is the soup made with meat stock?
phrases.note: Soups and sauces can hide meat or fish.

phrases.en: Do you have anything gluten-free?
Could I have it without the cheese, please?
phrases.he: אפשר לקבל את זה בלי הגבינה, בבקשה?

phrases.en: Can you hold the onions?
phrases.note: 'Hold the...' means 'leave it out'. Common in US diners and cafés; in the UK say 'without onions'.

phrases.en: Sorry, what's 'aubergine'?
phrases.note: Aubergine (UK) = eggplant (US) = חציל. Asking about menu words is completely normal.

phrases.en: What would you recommend?
I'll have the mushroom risotto, please.
phrases.he: אני אקח את ריזוטו הפטריות, בבקשה.

model_dialogue.speaker: partner
model_dialogue.text: Hi there, are you ready to order, or do you need a few more minutes?

model_dialogue.speaker: you
model_dialogue.text: I think we're ready. Just a quick question first: what's in the chicken salad?

model_dialogue.speaker: partner
model_dialogue.text: It's grilled chicken, mixed leaves and avocado, with a honey-mustard dressing and toasted walnuts on top.

model_dialogue.speaker: you
model_dialogue.text: Ah, I'm allergic to nuts. Could I have it without the walnuts? It's quite a serious allergy.

model_dialogue.speaker: partner
model_dialogue.text: Of course. I'll let the kitchen know so they can prepare it separately. Anything else you can't have?

model_dialogue.speaker: you
model_dialogue.text: No, just nuts, thanks. And my friend is vegetarian. Do you have any vegetarian mains?

model_dialogue.speaker: partner
model_dialogue.text: Yes, the mushroom risotto and the aubergine curry are both vegetarian. The risotto's made with vegetable stock.

model_dialogue.speaker: you
model_dialogue.text: Perfect. She'll have the risotto, then.

model_dialogue.speaker: partner
model_dialogue.text: Lovely. And anything to drink?

model_dialogue.speaker: you
model_dialogue.text: Two sparkling waters, please.

model_dialogue.speaker: partner
model_dialogue.text: Great, I'll be right back with those.

practice.partner: Are you ready to order?

options.text: Almost. Could I ask what's in the chicken salad first?

feedback.en: Natural and polite: 'Could I ask...' softens the question, and 'first' tells the server you'll order right after.
feedback.he: טבעי ומנומס: Could I ask מרכך את השאלה, ו-first מבהיר שתזמינו מיד אחרי התשובה.

options.text: Yes. What is in the chicken salad?

feedback.en: Clear and correct, but a bit abrupt. A short opener like 'Just a quick question' sounds friendlier.
feedback.he: ברור ותקין, אבל קצת חד. פתיחה קצרה כמו Just a quick question נשמעת ידידותית יותר.

options.text: Tell me what is inside the salad.

feedback.en: This is an order, not a question, so it sounds rude. In English, requests to staff are usually questions: 'Could you tell me...?'
feedback.he: זו פקודה ולא שאלה, ולכן היא נשמעת גסה. באנגלית פונים לצוות בשאלה: Could you tell me...?

model_replies: Almost. Could I ask what's in the chicken salad first?
Just a quick question first: what comes in the chicken salad?

practice.partner: It comes with grilled chicken, avocado and toasted walnuts.

options.text: I have allergy from nuts.

feedback.en: Two errors: you need 'an allergy' (with an article), and the preposition is 'to', not 'from'. Say: I'm allergic to nuts / I have a nut allergy.
feedback.he: שתי טעויות: צריך an allergy (עם an), ומילת היחס היא to ולא from. אפשר לומר I'm allergic to nuts או I have a nut allergy.

options.text: Oh, I'm allergic to nuts. Could I have it without the walnuts, please?

feedback.en: Says the problem clearly and asks for a solution politely. Note the preposition: allergic to.
feedback.he: מציג את הבעיה בבירור ומבקש פתרון בנימוס. שימו לב למילת היחס: allergic to.

options.text: I can't eat nuts. No walnuts, please.

feedback.en: Understandable, but 'can't eat' may sound like a preference. The word 'allergic' tells the kitchen to take real care.
feedback.he: מובן, אבל can't eat יכול להישמע כמו העדפה אישית. המילה allergic מבהירה למטבח שצריך להיזהר באמת.

model_replies: Oh, I'm allergic to nuts. Could I have it without the walnuts, please?
I have a nut allergy, so could you leave out the walnuts?

practice.partner: Is it a serious allergy?

options.text: Yes, very serious.

feedback.en: Clear, but very short. Adding a request, like 'Could you check with the kitchen?', helps the server act on it.
feedback.he: ברור, אבל קצר מאוד. בקשה נוספת כמו Could you check with the kitchen? עוזרת למלצרית לדעת מה לעשות.

options.text: No problem, it's fine.

feedback.en: This tells the server there's nothing to worry about, which could be dangerous if the allergy is real. Be clear and honest about it.
feedback.he: התשובה הזאת אומרת למלצרית שאין מה לדאוג, וזה עלול להיות מסוכן אם האלרגיה אמיתית. חשוב להיות ברורים וכנים.

options.text: Yes, it's quite serious. Could you check with the kitchen, please?

feedback.en: Honest about how serious it is, and asks the server to act. 'Check with the kitchen' is a very useful phrase.
feedback.he: אומר בכנות עד כמה זה חמור ומבקש פעולה. check with the kitchen הוא צירוף שימושי מאוד במסעדות.

model_replies: Yes, it's quite serious. Could you check with the kitchen, please?
Yes, it's a severe allergy. Even a tiny amount can make me ill.

practice.partner: And what can I get for your friend?

options.text: She's vegetarian. Which of the mains would you recommend?

feedback.en: Gives the key information first, then asks for a recommendation. 'Mains' is the usual British word for main courses.
feedback.he: קודם המידע החשוב, ואחר כך בקשה להמלצה. mains היא המילה הבריטית הרגילה למנות עיקריות.

options.text: She is vegetarian person, bring her something without meat.

feedback.en: 'Vegetarian person' needs 'a' (or just say 'She's vegetarian'), and 'bring her...' sounds like an order.
feedback.he: חסר a לפני vegetarian person (או פשוט She's vegetarian), ו-bring her... נשמע כמו פקודה.

options.text: She doesn't eat meat. What do you have?

feedback.en: Clear, but 'What do you have?' is very general. Ask about something specific: 'Which mains are vegetarian?'
feedback.he: ברור, אבל What do you have? כללי מדי. עדיף לשאול שאלה ממוקדת: Which mains are vegetarian?

model_replies: She's vegetarian. Which of the mains would you recommend?
She's vegetarian. Which dishes are vegetarian, apart from the salads?

practice.partner: The risotto's made with chicken stock, I'm afraid, but the curry is completely vegetarian.

options.text: OK, the curry then.

feedback.en: Natural in quick speech, but adding 'please' makes it more polite.
feedback.he: טבעי בדיבור מהיר, אבל please יוסיף נימוס.

options.text: Ah, OK. Then she'll have the curry, please. Is it very spicy?

feedback.en: Accepts the information, orders clearly with 'She'll have...', and checks one more detail.
feedback.he: מקבל את המידע, מזמין בבירור עם She'll have... ובודק עוד פרט חשוב.

options.text: OK, I want curry for she.

feedback.en: 'For she' should be 'for her' (object pronoun), and 'I want' sounds demanding when ordering. Try: 'She'll have the curry, please.'
feedback.he: צריך for her ולא for she (כינוי מושא), ו-I want נשמע תובעני בהזמנה. עדיף: She'll have the curry, please.

model_replies: Ah, OK. Then she'll have the curry, please.
In that case, she'll go for the curry. Is it very spicy?

roleplay.persona: Martha, an experienced, friendly server at a busy London bistro. She's quick and efficient, uses British words (starter, main, chips) and appreciates clear answers because the kitchen is very busy tonight.
roleplay.complication: The dish the learner wants comes with a sauce that 'may contain traces of nuts', so Martha has to check with the chef. She also mentions that the vegetarian lasagne has sold out, so the learner must choose something else for their friend.
roleplay.opening_line: Hi, sorry about the wait, it's a busy one tonight! Are you ready to order, or do you need a couple more minutes?

culture.en: Servers in the UK and the US are used to allergy questions. Always say if it's an allergy (not just a preference) and how serious it is, so the kitchen can take extra care.
culture.he: מלצרים בבריטניה ובארצות הברית רגילים לשאלות על אלרגיות. תמיד אמרו אם מדובר באלרגיה (ולא רק בהעדפה) ועד כמה היא חמורה, כדי שהמטבח ייזהר במיוחד.

culture.en: Menus often mark dishes with (V) for vegetarian, (VG) for vegan and (GF) for gluten-free. If you're not sure, just ask: 'Is this suitable for vegetarians?'
culture.he: בתפריטים מסמנים לעיתים קרובות (V) למנה צמחונית, (VG) למנה טבעונית ו-(GF) למנה ללא גלוטן. אם לא בטוחים, פשוט שואלים: Is this suitable for vegetarians?

culture.en: In English, 'vegetarian' usually means no meat and no fish. Someone who eats fish but not meat may call themselves 'pescatarian'.
culture.he: באנגלית vegetarian פירושו בדרך כלל בלי בשר ובלי דגים. מי שאוכל דגים אבל לא בשר מכנה את עצמו לפעמים pescatarian.

variants.note: In the US an entrée is the main course; in French, and sometimes in the UK, the word means a starter.

scenarios.title_he: קיבלתם מנה לא נכונה: להתלונן בנימוס

situation.en: You're at a casual restaurant in Chicago with friends. You ordered a grilled chicken burger with no cheese, but the server brings you a beef burger with cheese. You're hungry, and your friends have already started eating.
situation.he: אתם במסעדה פשוטה בשיקגו עם חברים. הזמנתם המבורגר עוף על הגריל בלי גבינה, אבל המלצר מביא המבורגר בקר עם גבינה. אתם רעבים, והחברים כבר התחילו לאכול.

goal.en: Point out the mistake politely, explain what you ordered and agree on a solution: a new dish, something quicker, or taking it off the check.
goal.he: להעיר בנימוס על הטעות, להסביר מה הזמנתם ולהגיע לפתרון: מנה חדשה, משהו מהיר יותר או הורדת המנה מהחשבון.

scenarios.partner_role: server at a casual American restaurant

phrases.en: Excuse me, sorry, I think there's been a mistake with my order.
phrases.he: סליחה, נראה לי שהייתה טעות בהזמנה שלי.

phrases.en: Sorry, but this isn't what I ordered.
phrases.he: סליחה, אבל זה לא מה שהזמנתי.

phrases.en: I actually ordered the chicken burger, with no cheese.
phrases.he: בעצם הזמנתי את המבורגר העוף, בלי גבינה.
phrases.note: 'Actually' here politely corrects a misunderstanding. It doesn't mean 'current' (אקטואלי).

phrases.en: Would it be possible to change it?
Roughly how long will that take?
No worries, these things happen.
This is a bit cold. Could you warm it up, please?
phrases.he: זה קצת קר. אפשר לחמם את זה, בבקשה?

phrases.en: I asked for my steak medium, but this is quite rare.
phrases.he: ביקשתי את הסטייק מדיום, אבל הוא די נא.

phrases.en: Could you take it off the check, please?
phrases.he: אפשר להוריד את זה מהחשבון, בבקשה?

phrases.en: Could you take it off the bill, please?
phrases.he: אפשר להוריד את זה מהחשבון, בבקשה?

phrases.en: Don't worry about it, I'll just have this one.
Could I speak to the manager, please?
phrases.note: Use this only if the problem isn't solved; asking straight away can sound aggressive.

model_dialogue.speaker: you
model_dialogue.text: Excuse me, sorry to bother you.

model_dialogue.speaker: partner
model_dialogue.text: Sure, what can I do for you?

model_dialogue.speaker: you
model_dialogue.text: I think there's been a mix-up with my order. I asked for the chicken burger with no cheese, but this is beef with cheese.

model_dialogue.speaker: partner
model_dialogue.text: Oh, I'm so sorry about that! Let me check the ticket... You're right, that's our mistake.

model_dialogue.speaker: you
model_dialogue.text: No worries. Would it be possible to change it?

model_dialogue.speaker: partner
model_dialogue.text: Absolutely. I'll get the kitchen to make a new one right away. It should be about ten minutes.

model_dialogue.speaker: you
model_dialogue.text: OK, thanks. My friends have already started, so the sooner the better.

model_dialogue.speaker: partner
model_dialogue.text: Totally understand. I'll bring you some fries in the meantime, on the house.

model_dialogue.speaker: you
model_dialogue.text: Oh, that's really kind. Thank you.

model_dialogue.speaker: partner
model_dialogue.text: Of course. Sorry again for the mix-up.

practice.partner: Here you go: one beef burger with cheese. Enjoy!

options.text: This is wrong. I ordered chicken.

feedback.en: Correct, but 'This is wrong' sounds blunt. Starting with 'Sorry, I think...' makes the server more willing to help.
feedback.he: תקין, אבל This is wrong נשמע בוטה. פתיחה כמו Sorry, I think... גורמת למלצר לרצות לעזור לכם.

options.text: Sorry, I think there's been a mistake. I ordered the chicken burger with no cheese.

feedback.en: Polite and clear: 'Sorry, I think...' softens the complaint, and you say exactly what you ordered.
feedback.he: מנומס וברור: Sorry, I think... מרכך את התלונה, ואתם אומרים בדיוק מה הזמנתם.

options.text: What is this? I didn't order this!

feedback.en: This sounds angry and accusing. Mistakes happen, and a calm tone usually gets a faster fix.
feedback.he: זה נשמע כועס ומאשים. טעויות קורות, וטון רגוע בדרך כלל מביא לפתרון מהיר יותר.

model_replies: Sorry, I think there's been a mistake. I ordered the chicken burger with no cheese.
Excuse me, I don't think this is mine. I asked for the chicken burger, no cheese.

practice.partner: Oh no, I'm so sorry! Do you want me to ask the kitchen to make you a new one?

options.text: Yes, please, if that's OK. How long do you think it'll take?

feedback.en: Accepts the offer warmly and asks a useful follow-up question.
feedback.he: מקבל את ההצעה בחמימות ושואל שאלת המשך שימושית.

options.text: Yes, and I want it for free.

feedback.en: Demanding something free straight away sounds rude. Restaurants often offer something themselves; if not, you can ask politely at the end.
feedback.he: לדרוש משהו בחינם כבר בהתחלה נשמע גס. מסעדות מציעות לא פעם פיצוי בעצמן, ואם לא, אפשר לבקש בנימוס בסוף הארוחה.

options.text: Yes. Quickly, please.

feedback.en: Understandable, but 'Quickly, please' can sound like pressure. 'How long will it take?' asks the same thing more politely.
feedback.he: מובן, אבל Quickly, please עלול להישמע כמו לחץ. How long will it take? שואל את אותו הדבר בנימוס.

model_replies: Yes, please, if that's OK. How long do you think it'll take?
That would be great, thanks. Will it take long?

practice.partner: It'll be about fifteen minutes, I'm afraid. The kitchen's pretty busy right now.

options.text: Fifteen minutes? That's ridiculous.

feedback.en: 'Ridiculous' is a very strong word and sounds rude to someone who is trying to help.
feedback.he: ridiculous ('מגוחך') היא מילה חריפה מאוד, והיא נשמעת גסה כלפי מי שמנסה לעזור.

options.text: OK.

feedback.en: Fine if you're happy to wait, but you miss the chance to explain your situation or ask for another option.
feedback.he: בסדר אם אין לכם בעיה לחכות, אבל מפספסים את ההזדמנות להסביר את המצב או לבקש חלופה.

options.text: Hmm, my friends have already started. Is there anything quicker I could have instead?

feedback.en: Explains your situation calmly and asks for an alternative instead of complaining.
feedback.he: מסביר את המצב ברוגע ומבקש חלופה במקום להתלונן.

model_replies: Hmm, my friends have already started. Is there anything quicker I could have instead?
That's a bit long for me. Is there something quicker on the menu?

practice.partner: We could do a chicken salad instead. That'd only take about five minutes.

options.text: That sounds great. I'll have the salad, then. Thanks for your help.

feedback.en: 'That sounds great' accepts naturally, and thanking the server ends the problem on a good note.
feedback.he: That sounds great היא דרך טבעית להסכים, והתודה סוגרת את העניין באווירה טובה.

options.text: Fine. Give me the salad.

feedback.en: It works, but 'Give me' sounds like an order. 'I'll have the salad' is the normal way to order.
feedback.he: זה עובד, אבל Give me נשמע כמו פקודה. הדרך הרגילה להזמין היא I'll have the salad.

options.text: I am agree, the salad is good for me.

feedback.en: 'I am agree' is a common mistake: 'agree' is a verb, so say 'I agree'. Here, 'That sounds good' is more natural anyway.
feedback.he: I am agree היא טעות נפוצה אצל דוברי עברית ('אני מסכים'): agree הוא פועל, ולכן אומרים I agree. וכאן That sounds good טבעי יותר בכל מקרה.

model_replies: That sounds great. I'll have the salad, then. Thanks for your help.
Perfect, the salad's fine. Thanks for sorting it out.

practice.partner: Here's your check. I took the burger off, and the salad's on us. Sorry again!

options.text: Finally. Next time be more careful.

feedback.en: This sounds rude, especially after they've apologized and fixed the problem.
feedback.he: נשמע גס, במיוחד אחרי שהם התנצלו ותיקנו את הבעיה.

options.text: Oh, that's really kind of you, thanks. No harm done!

feedback.en: Warm and gracious. 'No harm done' tells them the problem is forgotten.
feedback.he: חם ואדיב. No harm done אומר שהעניין נשכח ואין טינה.

options.text: OK, thank you.

feedback.en: Polite, but a warmer reply shows you appreciate the gesture.
feedback.he: מנומס, אבל תשובה חמה יותר מראה שאתם מעריכים את המחווה.

model_replies: Oh, that's really kind of you, thanks. No harm done!
That's very kind, thank you. You fixed it really quickly.

roleplay.persona: Tyler, a cheerful but overworked server at a busy diner in Chicago. He's friendly and apologetic, talks fast and uses casual American English ('No problem!', 'Totally!', 'you guys').
roleplay.complication: When the learner points out the mistake, Tyler first says the ticket shows 'cheeseburger' and asks if they're sure. Once the learner explains calmly, he checks, apologizes and offers a new burger that will take 20 minutes, or something quicker.
roleplay.opening_line: Alright, here we go: one cheeseburger! Can I get you anything else?

culture.en: In the US and the UK, politely pointing out a mistake is normal. Staff would usually rather fix the problem than have you leave unhappy, and a calm, specific complaint ('I ordered X, but this is Y') works best.
culture.he: בארצות הברית ובבריטניה מקובל לגמרי להעיר בנימוס על טעות. הצוות בדרך כלל מעדיף לתקן את הבעיה ולא שתצאו מאוכזבים, ותלונה רגועה ומדויקת (I ordered X, but this is Y) עובדת הכי טוב.

culture.en: British people often complain very gently: 'Sorry, I think this might be the wrong dish.' It can sound indirect to Israeli ears, but it's the norm, and it isn't a sign of weakness.
culture.he: בריטים מתלוננים לעיתים קרובות בעדינות רבה: Sorry, I think this might be the wrong dish. לאוזן ישראלית זה עלול להישמע עקיף, אבל זו הנורמה, ואין בזה שום חולשה.

variants.note: Both are understood everywhere; 'server' is more common in the US.

scenarios.title_en: Splitting the bill and tipping: US vs UK
scenarios.title_he: חלוקת החשבון וטיפים: ארצות הברית מול בריטניה

situation.en: You've just finished dinner with two friends at a restaurant in New York. You want to split the check, pay by card and leave the right tip. Next month you'll do the same in London, where the customs are a little different.
situation.he: סיימתם הרגע ארוחת ערב עם שני חברים במסעדה בניו יורק. אתם רוצים לחלק את החשבון, לשלם בכרטיס ולהשאיר טיפ מתאים. בחודש הבא תעשו את אותו הדבר בלונדון, שם המנהגים קצת שונים.

goal.en: Ask for the check/bill, arrange to pay separately or split it evenly, find out whether service is included and tip appropriately.
goal.he: לבקש את החשבון, לשלם בנפרד או לחלק שווה בשווה, לברר אם השירות כלול ולהשאיר טיפ מתאים.

scenarios.partner_role: server (in the US and in the UK)

phrases.en: Could we get the check, please?
Could we have the bill, please?
Could we pay separately?
phrases.note: Each person pays for what they had.

phrases.en: Can we get separate checks?
phrases.note: US servers often ask: 'All together or separate?'

phrases.note: = divide the total equally between three people.

phrases.en: Let's just split it evenly.
Is service included?
phrases.note: Very useful in the UK, where a service charge is often added to the bill.

phrases.en: Can I put the tip on the card?
Don't worry, it's on me.
Shall we go halves?
phrases.note: Mainly British. In the US: 'Want to split it?'

phrases.en: Keep the change.
phrases.note: Used when paying cash; the extra money is the tip.

model_dialogue.speaker: partner
model_dialogue.text: How was everything tonight?

model_dialogue.speaker: you
model_dialogue.text: It was delicious, thanks. Could we get the check, please?

model_dialogue.speaker: partner
model_dialogue.text: Sure thing. All on one check, or separate?

model_dialogue.speaker: you
model_dialogue.text: Could you split it three ways, please? We're all paying by card.

model_dialogue.speaker: partner
model_dialogue.text: No problem. So that's three equal checks, before tip.

model_dialogue.speaker: you
model_dialogue.text: Great. Can I put the tip on the card?

model_dialogue.speaker: partner
model_dialogue.text: Yep, the card machine will show you a few tip options, or you can enter your own amount.

model_dialogue.speaker: you
model_dialogue.text: Perfect. And just to check, is service included?

model_dialogue.speaker: partner
model_dialogue.text: Not for a table of three. We only add it automatically for groups of six or more.

model_dialogue.speaker: you
model_dialogue.text: Got it. Thanks so much, everything was great.

practice.partner: Can I get you guys anything else, or are you all set?

options.text: We're all set, thanks. Could we get the check, please?

feedback.en: 'All set' answers the question naturally, and 'check' is the usual American word.
feedback.he: All set עונה על השאלה באופן טבעי, ו-check היא המילה האמריקאית הרגילה לחשבון.

options.text: Give us the account, please.

feedback.en: 'Account' means a bank account, not a restaurant bill. Say 'the check' (US) or 'the bill' (UK).
feedback.he: account הוא חשבון בבנק, לא חשבון במסעדה. אומרים the check (ארצות הברית) או the bill (בריטניה).

options.text: No more food. The bill, please.

feedback.en: Understandable, but a bit clipped. In the US 'check' is more common, though 'bill' is understood.
feedback.he: מובן, אבל קצת קטוע. בארצות הברית check נפוץ יותר, אם כי גם bill מובן.

model_replies: We're all set, thanks. Could we get the check, please?
Nothing else, thanks. Can we get the check when you have a moment?

practice.partner: Is this all on one check, or are you splitting it?

options.text: Separate.

feedback.en: Clear, but one word sounds abrupt. Also, 'separate checks' means each person pays for what they ordered, which isn't the same as splitting equally.
feedback.he: ברור, אבל מילה אחת נשמעת חדה. וגם: separate checks פירושו שכל אחד משלם על מה שהזמין, וזה לא כמו חלוקה שווה.

options.text: We want to divide it to three.

feedback.en: 'Divide it to three' is a literal translation, and 'We want' sounds demanding. Say 'Could you split it three ways?'
feedback.he: divide it to three הוא תרגום מילולי, ו-We want נשמע תובעני. אומרים: Could you split it three ways?

options.text: Could you split it three ways, please?

feedback.en: Clear and polite. 'Split it three ways' means everyone pays the same amount.
feedback.he: ברור ומנומס. split it three ways פירושו שכל אחד משלם אותו סכום.

model_replies: Could you split it three ways, please?
Separate checks, please. We each had different things.

practice.partner: The card machine will ask you about the tip. Just pick whatever works for you.

options.text: No tip. The food was normal.

feedback.en: In the US, leaving no tip at a sit-down restaurant sends a strong negative message about the service. Also, 'normal' sounds odd as a comment on food; say 'OK' or 'fine'.
feedback.he: בארצות הברית, לא להשאיר טיפ במסעדה עם שירות לשולחן משדר ביקורת חריפה על השירות. וגם normal (תרגום של 'נורמלי') נשמע מוזר כתיאור של אוכל; אומרים OK או fine.

options.text: OK, I'll put 10 percent.

feedback.en: Grammatically fine, though 'go with' or 'leave' is more natural than 'put'. For good service at a sit-down restaurant in the US, 10% may come across as low.
feedback.he: תקין דקדוקית, אם כי go with או leave טבעיים יותר מ-put. על שירות טוב במסעדה בארצות הברית, 10% עלול להיתפס כנמוך.

options.text: Thanks. We'll go with 20 percent. You've been great.

feedback.en: Natural: 'go with' means 'choose'. At sit-down restaurants in the US, around 18-20% is a common choice for good service.
feedback.he: טבעי: go with פירושו 'לבחור'. במסעדות עם שירות לשולחן בארצות הברית, טיפ של כ-18-20% הוא בחירה נפוצה על שירות טוב.

model_replies: Thanks. We'll go with 20 percent. You've been great.
Thanks so much. I'll leave 20 percent; the service was excellent.

practice.partner: Here's your bill. Just so you know, a 12.5% service charge has been added.

options.text: Thanks for letting me know. So the tip's already included, right?

feedback.en: Polite, and checks your understanding. In the UK, if there's a service charge on the bill, you don't need to tip again.
feedback.he: מנומס ומוודא שהבנתם. בבריטניה, אם על החשבון כבר יש דמי שירות, לא צריך להוסיף טיפ.

options.text: OK. Is that instead of a tip?

feedback.en: A sensible question, but quite direct. 'So the tip's already included, right?' sounds friendlier.
feedback.he: שאלה הגיונית, אבל די ישירה. So the tip's already included, right? נשמע ידידותי יותר.

options.text: Why did you add money? I didn't ask for this.

feedback.en: This sounds accusing. Service charges are common in UK restaurants. They're usually optional, so if the service was poor, you can politely ask for it to be removed.
feedback.he: זה נשמע מאשים. דמי שירות נפוצים במסעדות בבריטניה. בדרך כלל הם לא חובה, כך שאם השירות היה גרוע אפשר לבקש בנימוס להוריד אותם.

model_replies: Thanks for letting me know. So the tip's already included, right?
Great, thanks. So we don't need to leave anything extra?

practice.partner: Are you paying by card? I'll bring the machine over.

options.text: Yes. Three cards.

feedback.en: The waiter will probably understand, but it's very short. 'Could we pay separately?' is clearer.
feedback.he: המלצר כנראה יבין, אבל זה קצר מאוד. Could we pay separately? ברור יותר.

options.text: Yes, please. Could we pay separately? Two of us are paying by card and one in cash.

feedback.en: Tells the waiter exactly how you'll pay before they bring the machine, which saves everyone time.
feedback.he: אומר למלצר בדיוק איך תשלמו עוד לפני שהוא מביא את המכשיר, וחוסך זמן לכולם.

options.text: Yes, but every one pays alone.

feedback.en: 'Every one pays alone' is a literal translation and sounds odd. The phrase is 'pay separately'.
feedback.he: every one pays alone הוא תרגום מילולי ונשמע מוזר. הביטוי הנכון הוא pay separately.

model_replies: Yes, please. Could we pay separately? Two of us are paying by card and one in cash.
Yes, please. We'd like to pay separately, if that's OK.

roleplay.persona: Priya, a calm, efficient waitress at a busy London restaurant. She's polite in a typically understated British way and happy to explain how the bill works, but she has several tables waiting.
roleplay.complication: One friend only had a starter, so splitting the bill equally isn't fair, and the learner must arrange a different split. The bill also includes a 12.5% service charge, which the learner should notice and ask about before adding a tip.
roleplay.opening_line: Here's your bill. Are you paying all together, or would you like to split it?

culture.en: In the US, tipping at sit-down restaurants is expected in practice. Many people leave roughly 15-20% of the bill, more for great service, and card machines often suggest percentages on the screen.
culture.he: בארצות הברית, במסעדות עם שירות לשולחן, טיפ הוא דבר מצופה בפועל. רבים משאירים בערך 15-20% מהחשבון, ויותר על שירות מצוין, ומכשירי האשראי מציעים לרוב אחוזים על המסך.

culture.en: In the UK, many restaurants add a service charge (often around 10-12.5%) to the bill. It's usually optional, and if it's there you don't need to tip again. Without it, about 10% is a common tip for good service. When you order at a counter, a tip isn't usually expected.
culture.he: בבריטניה, מסעדות רבות מוסיפות לחשבון דמי שירות (לרוב בסביבות 10-12.5%). בדרך כלל זה לא חובה, ואם זה כבר בחשבון לא צריך להוסיף טיפ. בלי דמי שירות, כ-10% הוא טיפ מקובל על שירות טוב. כשמזמינים בדלפק, בדרך כלל לא מצופה להשאיר טיפ.

culture.en: Customs change over time and from place to place. If you're unsure, it's fine to ask politely: 'Is service included?'
culture.he: המנהגים משתנים עם הזמן וממקום למקום. אם לא בטוחים, זה בסדר גמור לשאול בנימוס: Is service included?

variants.note: 'Could we pay separately?' works in both.
Both are informal; 'go halves' is mainly British.
In the UK, the tip may already be on the bill as a service charge.

scenarios.title_en: At the counter: ordering and small talk

situation.en: It's a sunny morning in Brighton, on the south coast of England. You order at the counter of a small café, and the barista is chatty and asks where you're from.
situation.he: בוקר שמשי בברייטון, בחוף הדרומי של אנגליה. אתם מזמינים בדלפק של בית קפה קטן, והבריסטה, שאוהב לדבר, שואל מאיפה אתם.

goal.en: Order a drink and something to eat, answer 'eat in or take away?', and have a short, friendly chat with the person serving you.
goal.he: להזמין שתייה ומשהו לאכול, לענות על השאלה אם זה לשבת או לקחת, ולנהל שיחה קצרה וידידותית עם מי שמגיש לכם.

phrases.en: Hi, can I get a flat white, please?
phrases.note: 'Can I get...?' is very common in cafés, especially in the US. 'Could I have...?' is a little more formal.

phrases.en: Could I have a cappuccino and a croissant, please?
Do you have oat milk?
For here, please.
phrases.note: Answer to 'For here or to go?'

phrases.en: To go, please.
To take away, please.
phrases.note: Answer to 'Eat in or take away?'

phrases.en: Just a small one, thanks.
It's my first time in Brighton.
I'm from Israel, near Tel Aviv.
Any tips for things to do around here?
phrases.he: יש לך המלצות מה לעשות באזור?

phrases.en: Cheers!
phrases.note: In the UK, 'Cheers' often just means 'thanks' or 'bye'.

phrases.en: Have a good one!
phrases.note: A friendly goodbye, very common in the US.

practice.partner: Hiya, what can I get you?

options.text: I would like to order one cappuccino, please.

feedback.en: Correct, but a bit formal and long for a café. 'Can I get a cappuccino, please?' sounds more relaxed.
feedback.he: תקין, אבל קצת רשמי וארוך לבית קפה. Can I get a cappuccino, please? נשמע משוחרר יותר.

options.text: Give me cappuccino.

feedback.en: With no 'please' and no question, this sounds rude. It also needs 'a': a cappuccino.
feedback.he: בלי please ובלי שאלה זה נשמע גס. וחסר גם a: a cappuccino.

options.text: Hi! Can I get a cappuccino, please?

feedback.en: A friendly greeting plus a short, polite request. Perfect for a café counter.
feedback.he: ברכה ידידותית ובקשה קצרה ומנומסת. מושלם לדלפק של בית קפה.

model_replies: Hi! Can I get a cappuccino, please?
Hi, could I have a small cappuccino, please?

practice.partner: Is that to have in or take away?

options.text: To have in, please.

feedback.en: Answers with the same words as the question: simple and natural.
feedback.he: עונה באותן מילים שבשאלה: פשוט וטבעי.

options.text: Yes.

feedback.en: This is an 'or' question, so 'yes' doesn't answer it. Choose one of the options: 'To have in' or 'Take away'.
feedback.he: זו שאלת 'או', ולכן yes לא עונה עליה. בוחרים אחת האפשרויות: To have in או Take away.

options.text: Inside.

feedback.en: Understandable, but 'inside' could also mean you want an indoor table. Use the words from the question: 'To have in, please.'
feedback.he: מובן, אבל inside יכול להתפרש גם כבקשה לשולחן בפנים. עדיף להשתמש במילים מהשאלה: To have in, please.

model_replies: To have in, please.
Take away, please.

practice.partner: Lovely day, isn't it?

options.text: Yes.

feedback.en: Polite, but it ends the conversation. Add a short comment: 'Yes, it's beautiful!'
feedback.he: מנומס, אבל סוגר את השיחה. כדאי להוסיף הערה קצרה: Yes, it's beautiful!

options.text: It's gorgeous! Much warmer than I expected.

feedback.en: Agreeing and adding a small comment keeps the small talk going. British people love talking about the weather.
feedback.he: הסכמה עם הערה קטנה משאירה את השיחה זורמת. בריטים אוהבים לדבר על מזג האוויר.

options.text: No, in Israel the weather is much better.

feedback.en: The grammar is fine, but arguing about the weather, or saying home is better, can sound rude. Small talk is about being friendly, not being right.
feedback.he: הדקדוק תקין, אבל להתווכח על מזג האוויר, או לומר שבבית יותר טוב, עלול להישמע גס. בשיחת חולין המטרה היא להיות נחמדים, לא לצדוק.

model_replies: It's gorgeous! Much warmer than I expected.
It really is! Perfect weather for a walk by the sea.

practice.partner: So, are you here on holiday?

options.text: Yes. I am in a trip of one week.

feedback.en: 'In a trip' should be 'on a trip', and 'a trip of one week' is a literal translation. Say 'I'm here for a week.'
feedback.he: צריך on a trip ולא in a trip, ו-a trip of one week הוא תרגום מילולי. אומרים: I'm here for a week.

options.text: Yeah, just for a week. It's my first time in the UK.

feedback.en: Relaxed and natural, and it gives the barista something to respond to.
feedback.he: משוחרר וטבעי, ונותן לבריסטה על מה להגיב.

options.text: Yes, I am on a holiday.

feedback.en: Understood, but in British English it's 'on holiday', with no 'a' (in the US: 'on vacation'). 'Yeah, just for a week' also sounds more relaxed.
feedback.he: מובן, אבל באנגלית בריטית אומרים on holiday, בלי a (ובארצות הברית: on vacation). וגם Yeah, just for a week נשמע משוחרר יותר.

model_replies: Yeah, just for a week. It's my first time in the UK.
Yes, I'm here for a week with my family.

practice.partner: That's four twenty, please. Card or cash?

options.text: Card, please. Thanks, have a lovely day!

feedback.en: Answers the question and ends with a friendly goodbye.
feedback.he: עונה על השאלה ומסיים בפרידה ידידותית.

options.text: Card.

feedback.en: Clear, but abrupt. Add 'please' and a friendly goodbye.
feedback.he: ברור, אבל חד. כדאי להוסיף please ופרידה ידידותית.

options.text: Four twenty? Why so expensive?

feedback.en: Commenting on the price to the barista sounds rude; they don't set the prices. If something is too expensive, just change your order politely.
feedback.he: להעיר לבריסטה על המחיר נשמע גס, כי לא הוא קובע את המחירים. אם משהו יקר מדי, פשוט משנים את ההזמנה בנימוס.

model_replies: Card, please. Thanks, have a lovely day!
Card, please. Cheers!

roleplay.persona: Jake, a laid-back barista in his twenties at an independent café in Brighton. He's chatty and curious about visitors, uses casual British English ('Hiya', 'cheers', 'lovely') and loves recommending local spots.
roleplay.complication: The café has just run out of the pastry the learner asks for, so Jake suggests something else. While making the coffee, he asks a few friendly small-talk questions: where they're from, how long they're staying and what they've seen so far.
roleplay.opening_line: Hiya! What can I get you this morning?

culture.en: In the UK and the US, a little friendly small talk with café staff is normal: the weather, your plans, where you're from. Keep it short, especially if there's a queue (UK) or a line (US) behind you.
culture.he: בבריטניה ובארצות הברית מקובל לנהל שיחת חולין קצרה עם צוות בית הקפה: מזג האוויר, התוכניות שלכם, מאיפה אתם. רק כדאי לקצר, במיוחד כשיש תור מאחוריכם.

culture.en: In many British cafés you order and pay at the counter, then sit down, and sometimes they bring the food to your table. If you're not sure, ask: 'Do I order here?'
culture.he: בהרבה בתי קפה בבריטניה מזמינים ומשלמים בדלפק, ואז מתיישבים, ולפעמים מביאים את האוכל לשולחן. אם לא בטוחים, שואלים: Do I order here?

culture.en: At a bar counter the same phrases work: 'Can I get a lemonade, please?' In the US, people usually leave the bartender a small tip, even for soft drinks; in the UK, tipping at the bar isn't usually expected.
culture.he: בדלפק של בר עובדים אותם ביטויים: Can I get a lemonade, please? בארצות הברית נהוג להשאיר לברמן טיפ קטן, גם על משקאות קלים; בבריטניה בדרך כלל לא מצופה טיפ בבר.

variants.note: Typical rather than exclusive: you'll hear both in both countries.

scenarios.title_en: A friendly chat at a beach bar

situation.en: You're on holiday with your family in Portugal. It's late afternoon, and you're relaxing at a beach bar with a lemonade. A traveller about your age asks if the seat next to you is free, and you start chatting.
situation.he: אתם בחופשה משפחתית בפורטוגל. שעת אחר צהריים מאוחרת, ואתם נחים בבר על החוף עם לימונדה. מטיילת בערך בגילכם שואלת אם הכיסא לידכם פנוי, ואתם מתחילים לדבר.

goal.en: Start a friendly conversation with a stranger: ask and answer questions about your trips, introduce yourselves, share a tip and end the chat naturally.
goal.he: לפתוח שיחה ידידותית עם מישהי זרה: לשאול ולענות על שאלות על הטיול, להציג את עצמכם, לשתף המלצה ולסיים את השיחה בצורה טבעית.

scenarios.partner_role: another traveller at a beach bar

model_dialogue.speaker: you
model_dialogue.text: Nice to meet you too, Sam. Enjoy the sunset!

practice.partner: Hi, sorry, is this seat taken?

options.text: Yes, sit.

feedback.en: Confusing: 'Yes' means the seat IS taken, but then you say 'sit'. Answer the question exactly: 'No, it's free.'
feedback.he: מבלבל: yes פירושו שהכיסא תפוס, ואז אתם אומרים sit. עונים בדיוק על השאלה: No, it's free.

options.text: No, it's free. Go ahead!

feedback.en: Friendly and natural. 'Go ahead' invites them to sit down.
feedback.he: ידידותי וטבעי. Go ahead מזמין לשבת.

options.text: No, it is not taken. You can sit.

feedback.en: Correct, but it sounds stiff. Contractions (it's) and 'Go ahead' sound warmer.
feedback.he: תקין, אבל נשמע נוקשה. קיצורים (it's) ו-Go ahead נשמעים חמים יותר.

model_replies: No, it's free. Go ahead!
Nope, have a seat!

practice.partner: So, are you here on vacation too?

options.text: Yeah, with my family for two weeks. What about you?

feedback.en: Answers briefly and asks back, which is the key to keeping small talk going.
feedback.he: עונה בקצרה ושואל בחזרה, וזה הסוד לשיחת חולין שזורמת.

options.text: Yes, I am in vacation with my family since two weeks.

feedback.en: Two errors: 'on vacation' (not 'in'), and 'for two weeks' (not 'since'). 'Since' needs a starting point: since Monday.
feedback.he: שתי טעויות: on vacation ולא in, ו-for two weeks ולא since. אחרי since באה נקודת התחלה: since Monday.

options.text: Yes.

feedback.en: True, but one word can make you seem uninterested, even if you're just shy. Add a detail and ask a question back.
feedback.he: נכון, אבל מילה אחת עלולה לגרום לכם להיראות לא מעוניינים, גם אם אתם פשוט ביישנים. הוסיפו פרט ושאלו בחזרה.

model_replies: Yeah, with my family for two weeks. What about you?
Yes, we're here for two weeks. How about you?

practice.partner: I'm from Toronto. I've been backpacking around Europe for a month.

options.text: Nice. I never was in Canada.

feedback.en: Friendly, but 'I never was' should be 'I've never been' (present perfect for life experience). It also turns the topic back to you; a question about her trip works better.
feedback.he: ידידותי, אבל במקום I never was צריך I've never been (present perfect לניסיון חיים). וזה גם מחזיר את השיחה אליכם; שאלה על הטיול שלה עדיפה.

options.text: How much costs a trip like that?

feedback.en: Wrong word order: 'How much does a trip like that cost?' And asking about money is too personal with someone you've just met.
feedback.he: סדר מילים שגוי: How much does a trip like that cost? וחוץ מזה, שאלה על כסף אישית מדי מול מישהו שזה עתה הכרתם.

options.text: Wow, a whole month! What's been the best place so far?

feedback.en: Shows real interest and asks an open question, so the other person can talk.
feedback.he: מראה עניין אמיתי ושואל שאלה פתוחה, שמזמינה את הצד השני לספר.

model_replies: Wow, a whole month! What's been the best place so far?
That sounds amazing. Where else have you been?

practice.partner: Have you been to Lisbon yet?

options.text: Not yet, we're going on Thursday. Is there anything I shouldn't miss?

feedback.en: 'Not yet' is the natural short answer, 'we're going' is right for a fixed plan, and asking for tips keeps the chat going.
feedback.he: Not yet היא התשובה הקצרה והטבעית, we're going מתאים לתוכנית שכבר נקבעה, ובקשת המלצה ממשיכה את השיחה.

options.text: No, not yet. We go there Thursday.

feedback.en: Understandable, but for a fixed plan use the present continuous: 'We're going on Thursday.' Americans sometimes drop 'on', but with 'on' it's always correct.
feedback.he: מובן, אבל לתוכנית שכבר נקבעה משתמשים בהווה מתמשך: We're going on Thursday. אמריקאים משמיטים לפעמים את on, אבל איתו זה תמיד נכון.

options.text: No, I didn't been there.

feedback.en: 'Didn't been' mixes two tenses. Say 'Not yet' or 'No, I haven't been there yet.'
feedback.he: didn't been מערבב שני זמנים. אומרים Not yet או No, I haven't been there yet.

model_replies: Not yet, we're going on Thursday. Is there anything I shouldn't miss?
No, not yet. We're going there at the end of the week. Any tips?

practice.partner: Anyway, my friends are waving at me. It was really nice talking to you!

options.text: OK, bye.

feedback.en: Not wrong, but it sounds cold after a friendly chat. Return the compliment first: 'You too!'
feedback.he: לא שגוי, אבל נשמע קר אחרי שיחה נעימה. קודם מחזירים מחמאה: You too!

options.text: Wait, give me your Instagram.

feedback.en: 'Give me' sounds like an order and can feel pushy. If you'd like to stay in touch, ask lightly ('Are you on Instagram?'), and only if you're both comfortable.
feedback.he: Give me נשמע כמו פקודה ועלול להרגיש לוחץ. אם רוצים להישאר בקשר, שואלים בקלילות (Are you on Instagram?), ורק אם שני הצדדים מרגישים בנוח.

options.text: You too! Enjoy the rest of your trip!

feedback.en: 'You too' returns the compliment, and the good wishes end the chat warmly.
feedback.he: You too מחזיר את המחמאה, והאיחול מסיים את השיחה בחום.

model_replies: You too! Enjoy the rest of your trip!
Same here! Have a great time in Lisbon.

roleplay.persona: Sam, a friendly 19-year-old woman from Toronto who is backpacking around Europe for the summer. She's easy-going, curious and a little talkative, and uses casual North American English ('awesome', 'for sure', 'super').
roleplay.complication: Sam mishears where the learner is from (she thinks they said 'Italy', not 'Israel') and starts talking about Italian food, so the learner must politely correct her. Later she asks for one place worth visiting in the learner's country, which the learner must describe briefly.
roleplay.opening_line: Hey, sorry, is anyone sitting here? It's packed today!

culture.en: Small talk with strangers usually stays on safe topics: travel, food, the weather, music, sport. With someone you've just met, avoid money, politics and religion.
culture.he: שיחת חולין עם זרים נשארת בדרך כלל בנושאים בטוחים: טיולים, אוכל, מזג אוויר, מוזיקה וספורט. מול מישהו שזה עתה הכרתם, עדיף להימנע מכסף, פוליטיקה ודת.

culture.en: Asking a question back ('How about you?', 'What about you?') is essential. One-word answers can make you seem uninterested, even if you're just shy.
culture.he: חשוב מאוד לשאול בחזרה (How about you?, What about you?). תשובות של מילה אחת עלולות לגרום לכם להיראות לא מעוניינים, גם אם אתם רק ביישנים.

culture.en: Be friendly but sensible: chat in public places, don't share where you're staying, and never feel you have to swap numbers or social media.
culture.he: היו ידידותיים אבל זהירים: שוחחו במקומות ציבוריים, אל תשתפו איפה אתם מתאכסנים, ואל תרגישו מחויבים להחליף מספרי טלפון או רשתות חברתיות.

situation.en: It's evening in New York. You take a yellow cab from Penn Station to your hotel near Central Park. You need to give the address, ask roughly how long it will take and how much it will cost, and sort out a small problem with paying.
situation.he: ערב בניו יורק. אתם לוקחים מונית צהובה מפן סטיישן למלון ליד סנטרל פארק. צריך למסור כתובת, לשאול בערך כמה זמן זה ייקח וכמה זה יעלה, ולפתור בעיה קטנה בתשלום.

goal.en: Give your destination clearly, ask about the route, time and fare, and solve a payment or drop-off problem politely.
goal.he: למסור את היעד בבירור, לשאול על המסלול, הזמן והמחיר, ולפתור בנימוס בעיה בתשלום או בנקודת ההורדה.

phrases.en: Hi, could you take me to the Park View Hotel on West 58th Street, please?
phrases.he: היי, למלון פארק ויו ברחוב 58 מערב, בבקשה.

phrases.en: How long will it take with this traffic?
phrases.he: כמה זמן זה ייקח עם הפקקים האלה?

phrases.en: Roughly how much will it be?
Is there a quicker way?
Hi, is this the Uber for Dana?
phrases.note: With rideshares, check the driver's name, the car and the plate number before you get in.

phrases.en: Could you turn the AC down a little?
phrases.note: In the UK: 'air con'.

phrases.en: Could you drop me off at the corner, please?
Just here is fine, thanks.
Sorry, the card machine doesn't seem to be working.
phrases.he: סליחה, נראה שמכשיר האשראי לא עובד.

phrases.en: Do you take cash? I've only got a fifty.
phrases.he: אפשר לשלם במזומן? יש לי רק שטר של חמישים.
phrases.note: Mention a large bill (UK: note) early, so the driver can check they have change.

phrases.en: Could I get a receipt, please?
Keep the change.

model_dialogue.speaker: you
model_dialogue.text: Hi, could you take me to the Park View Hotel on West 58th Street, please?

model_dialogue.speaker: partner
model_dialogue.text: Sure. Between which avenues?

model_dialogue.speaker: you
model_dialogue.text: Between Sixth and Seventh, I think. How long will it take?

model_dialogue.speaker: partner
model_dialogue.text: With this traffic? Maybe twenty-five minutes.

model_dialogue.speaker: you
model_dialogue.text: OK. And roughly how much will it be?

model_dialogue.speaker: partner
model_dialogue.text: It's on the meter, but probably around thirty bucks, plus tip.

model_dialogue.speaker: you
model_dialogue.text: Great, thanks... Oh, just here on the right is fine.

model_dialogue.speaker: partner
model_dialogue.text: OK, that's twenty-eight fifty.

model_dialogue.speaker: you
model_dialogue.text: Sorry, the card machine back here doesn't seem to be working.

model_dialogue.speaker: partner
model_dialogue.text: Ah, it does that sometimes. Give me a second... OK, try it now.

model_dialogue.speaker: you
model_dialogue.text: That worked. Could I get a receipt, please?

model_dialogue.speaker: partner
model_dialogue.text: Sure, it'll come up on the screen. Enjoy your stay!

practice.partner: Hi there. Where to?

options.text: Park View Hotel.

feedback.en: Drivers hear this a lot, so it works, but adding the street avoids confusion, and 'please' sounds friendlier.
feedback.he: נהגים שומעים את זה הרבה, אז זה עובד, אבל הוספת הרחוב מונעת בלבול, ו-please נשמע ידידותי יותר.

options.text: Hi, could you take me to the Park View Hotel on West 58th Street, please?

feedback.en: Polite, and the street name helps the driver find it quickly.
feedback.he: מנומס, ושם הרחוב עוזר לנהג למצוא את המקום מהר.

options.text: I want to arrive to the Park View Hotel.

feedback.en: 'Arrive to' is wrong (it's 'arrive at'), and 'I want to arrive' sounds unnatural here. Say 'Could you take me to...?' or just 'The Park View Hotel, please.'
feedback.he: arrive to שגוי (אומרים arrive at), ו-I want to arrive לא טבעי כאן. אומרים Could you take me to...? או פשוט The Park View Hotel, please.

model_replies: Hi, could you take me to the Park View Hotel on West 58th Street, please?
The Park View Hotel, please. It's on West 58th Street.

practice.partner: I can take the highway or go straight up through Midtown. The highway's longer, but there's less traffic. Your call.

options.text: Take the short way, and don't try to cheat me.

feedback.en: Accusing the driver of cheating is rude and may start an argument. If you're worried about the fare, just ask: 'Roughly how much will it be?'
feedback.he: להאשים את הנהג ברמאות זה גס ועלול להוביל לוויכוח. אם המחיר מדאיג אתכם, פשוט שואלים: Roughly how much will it be?

options.text: I don't know. You decide.

feedback.en: Acceptable, but it can sound a bit careless. 'Whichever's quicker is fine' gives the driver a clear instruction.
feedback.he: סביר, אבל עלול להישמע אדיש. Whichever's quicker is fine נותן לנהג הנחיה ברורה.

options.text: Whichever's quicker is fine. Roughly how much will it be?

feedback.en: Lets the driver choose but gives a clear priority, and checks the fare. 'Your call' means 'you decide'.
feedback.he: נותן לנהג לבחור אבל עם עדיפות ברורה, ובודק את המחיר. Your call פירושו 'ההחלטה שלך'.

model_replies: Whichever's quicker is fine. Roughly how much will it be?
Let's take the highway if it's faster. About how much will that be?

practice.partner: Sorry, I can't stop right outside the hotel. There's construction. Is the corner OK?

options.text: Sure, the corner's fine. Thanks for letting me know.

feedback.en: Flexible and polite: you accept the change and thank the driver.
feedback.he: גמיש ומנומס: מקבלים את השינוי ומודים לנהג.

options.text: No, you must stop in front of the hotel.

feedback.en: 'You must' sounds like an order, and the driver may not be allowed to stop there. Accept it, or ask politely: 'Could you get any closer?'
feedback.he: You must נשמע כמו פקודה, ויכול להיות שלנהג אסור לעצור שם. אפשר להסכים, או לשאול בנימוס: Could you get any closer?

options.text: This is acceptable for me.

feedback.en: Understandable, but far too formal for a taxi. Say 'Sure, the corner's fine.'
feedback.he: מובן, אבל רשמי מדי למונית. אומרים: Sure, the corner's fine.

model_replies: Sure, the corner's fine. Thanks for letting me know.
No problem, the corner works. Thanks.

practice.partner: Here we are. That's twenty-eight fifty. Just tap your card on the screen back there.

options.text: Your machine is broken.

feedback.en: Clear, but it sounds like blame. 'The card machine doesn't seem to be working' is softer.
feedback.he: ברור, אבל נשמע מאשים. The card machine doesn't seem to be working רך יותר.

options.text: Sorry, I've tried twice, but the card machine doesn't seem to be working. Could you check it?

feedback.en: 'Doesn't seem to be working' describes the problem politely without blaming anyone, and you ask for help.
feedback.he: doesn't seem to be working מתאר את הבעיה בנימוס בלי להאשים אף אחד, ומבקש עזרה.

options.text: The machine is broken, so I don't pay.

feedback.en: You still need to pay. Explain the problem and suggest another way: 'Could I pay in cash, or could you restart the machine?'
feedback.he: עדיין צריך לשלם. מסבירים את הבעיה ומציעים דרך אחרת: Could I pay in cash, or could you restart the machine?

model_replies: Sorry, I've tried twice, but the card machine doesn't seem to be working. Could you check it?
Sorry, my card isn't going through. Could you restart the machine?

practice.partner: Sorry about that. It's still not working. Can you pay cash?

options.text: I have no cash. It's your problem.

feedback.en: Rude, and it doesn't solve anything. Suggest a solution: 'I don't have enough cash. Is there an ATM nearby?'
feedback.he: גס, ולא פותר כלום. מציעים פתרון: I don't have enough cash. Is there an ATM nearby?

options.text: Yes. Here.

feedback.en: It works, but it sounds abrupt. 'Sure, here you go' is friendlier.
feedback.he: זה עובד, אבל נשמע חד. Sure, here you go ידידותי יותר.

options.text: Sure, here's thirty-five. Keep the change.

feedback.en: Natural: rounding up and saying 'Keep the change' is a simple way to tip in a US taxi. Here that's a tip of just over 20%.
feedback.he: טבעי: לעגל כלפי מעלה ולומר Keep the change היא דרך פשוטה להשאיר טיפ במונית בארצות הברית. כאן זה טיפ של קצת יותר מ-20%.

model_replies: Sure, here's thirty-five. Keep the change.
No problem, here you go. Keep the change.

roleplay.persona: Luis, a talkative New York taxi driver who has been driving for twenty years. He's friendly, proud of knowing every shortcut, talks quickly and likes chatting about the city and baseball.
roleplay.complication: Luis suggests a longer route that he says is 'faster at this time of day', and at the end the card reader in the back stops working, so the learner has to ask about other ways to pay.

culture.en: In New York, yellow cabs charge by the meter, and passengers usually add a tip, often around 15-20%. With rideshare apps the price is usually shown before you ride, and you can tip in the app.
culture.he: בניו יורק המוניות הצהובות גובות לפי מונה, ונוסעים בדרך כלל מוסיפים טיפ, לרוב בסביבות 15-20%. באפליקציות הסעות המחיר מוצג בדרך כלל מראש, ואפשר להוסיף טיפ באפליקציה.

culture.en: In London, you can stop a black cab in the street and it uses a meter, while a minicab has to be booked in advance. People often round up the fare instead of tipping a set percentage.
culture.he: בלונדון אפשר לעצור ברחוב מונית שחורה, והיא נוסעת לפי מונה, ואילו מיניקאב צריך להזמין מראש. נוהגים לעגל את הסכום כלפי מעלה במקום לתת טיפ באחוזים קבועים.

culture.en: Before getting into a rideshare, check the driver's name, the car and the plate number in the app. If they don't match, don't get in.
culture.he: לפני שנכנסים לרכב של אפליקציית הסעות, בודקים באפליקציה את שם הנהג, הרכב ומספר הרישוי. אם משהו לא תואם, לא נכנסים.

variants.note: A UK motorway is a major multi-lane road, like a US freeway or interstate.
'Taxi' is understood everywhere; 'cab' is more common in the US, and a London taxi is a 'black cab'.

scenarios.title_en: Metro and train: tickets, signs and announcements
scenarios.title_he: רכבת תחתית ורכבת: כרטיסים, שלטים והכרזות

situation.en: You're at Victoria station in London and need to get to King's Cross on the Underground. Later in the week you'll take a train to Brighton. You're not sure which ticket to buy, which line or platform to use, or what some announcements mean, so you ask a member of staff.
situation.he: אתם בתחנת ויקטוריה בלונדון וצריכים להגיע לקינגס קרוס ברכבת התחתית. בהמשך השבוע תיסעו ברכבת לברייטון. אתם לא בטוחים איזה כרטיס לקנות, באיזה קו או רציף להשתמש ומה אומרות חלק מההכרזות, ולכן אתם פונים לאחד מאנשי הצוות.

goal.en: Buy the right ticket (single or return), find the right line, direction and platform, and understand common signs and announcements.
goal.he: לקנות את הכרטיס המתאים (כיוון אחד או הלוך-חזור), למצוא את הקו, הכיוון והרציף הנכונים ולהבין שלטים והכרזות נפוצים.

scenarios.partner_role: station staff member / ticket office clerk

phrases.he: סליחה, איזה קו מגיע לקינגס קרוס?

phrases.he: אפשר פשוט להשתמש בכרטיס האשראי, או שצריך כרטיס נסיעה?

A one-way ticket to Boston, please.

Which platform does it leave from?

Mind the gap.
